description:
📝 Notes
Feb 23, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh, along with Noémi Biró, discussed defining a representative system "slice" for the new project focus, consolidating documentation under a "New Focus" Notion page, and clarifying the OS project as an effort to concretize the Research and Development direction rather than a pivot. The participants identified the need for a functional prototype within one month to engage potential partners and investors, outlining initial steps including crystallizing ideas, starting to build, and concurrently seeking funding from investors like Nikun Kotari and through consulting opportunities. The team also agreed to schedule two intensive sessions this week to define the specifications for the OS project, addressed the necessity for Gabor Kerekes to fix G-Cloud security and push analytics scripts for Amir Houieh to generate detailed user activity metrics for Noémi Biró, and considered financial operations including compensation structuring and website updates.
Details
Defining the Project Slice and Vision: Gabor Kerekes suggested devoting another session to distilling project ideas and defining a system "slice" that represents the whole vision without needing to build the entire system immediately, similar to the Pathfinder rebuild. This representative slice must manifest the 'mycelium layer' and include a few 'mushrooms'.
Consolidating Project Documentation on Notion: Amir Houieh mentioned they had already written extensive thoughts on the project, suggesting it would be beneficial to share these documents to aid Gabor Kerekes in organizing their thoughts. They discussed finding a location on Notion, deciding that a new page called "New Focus" under "Internal Projects Repos" would be appropriate for centralizing all related thoughts and linking documents, such as Amir Houieh's "adapt OS" notes (00:16:35).
Clarifying the Project Focus and Pivot: The discussion centered on how this new focus, referred to as the OS, represents a pivot from the original Research and Development (R&D) plan, centralizing all thoughts into one product idea (00:12:08). Gabor Kerekes clarified that it is less of a pivot and more an effort to make the R&D direction more concrete (00:13:17).
Identifying Potential Investors: The group discussed the need for financial sustainability, which led to a conversation about seeking investors who align with their core values (00:30:21). Gabor Kerekes mentioned an investor, Nikun Kotari, who is interested in augmenting cognition with AI and tools for deep thought, and wrote about 'token anxiety' (00:19:32). Amir Houieh shared their existing list of potential investors and mentioned A16Z as a major venture capital group that operates differently (00:21:05).
Criteria for the Ideal Investor: Gabor Kerekes argued that the technology they are developing goes against traditional technology monetization models, which focus on capturing attention for advertising value (00:24:11). They emphasized that the ideal investor must be driven by a conviction that this technology "needs to exist" to preserve humanity and work against the dehumanizing nature of technology, suggesting a more philanthropic investor persona who values the mission over a 1000x return (00:26:41).
Necessity of a Functional Prototype: The group agreed that a functional prototype is required to engage with potential partners and investors effectively, as ideas are now cheaper than ever (00:33:47). The consensus was that they need to "show, not tell" the value of their fundamentally different approach, aiming to build a prototype within one month (00:34:56).
Developing a Project Framework and Financial Strategy: The team discussed the need for a structure and framework to guide their efforts, especially regarding financial sustainability (00:28:57). Amir Houieh proposed that within two months of building a prototype, they should know if they have an investor who will allow them to go "full in" on the project after the current CBIL project concludes (00:36:00).
Outlining Initial Steps for the New Focus: The group agreed on three initial steps: first, crystallize the ideas enough to efficiently define the target for the agents; second, start building; and third, concurrently seek both investors and consulting opportunities to fund development (00:39:44). They also discussed seeking grants, with Noémi Biró noting there are no current open grants in Romania, and Amir Houieh mentioning they missed the deadline for some EU categories (00:41:24).
Scheduling and Timeline for Crystallizing Ideas: The immediate goal is to clarify and pin down the ideas, with Gabor Kerekes estimating that one or two focus sessions this week would be sufficient to start building (00:48:18). The team scheduled two intensive sessions for the week to define the common understanding and specifications for the "OS" project, which will occur on Tuesday and Wednesday after their daily meetings (00:57:47).
Handling Compensation and Financial Operations: The team discussed the financial aspect of the CBIL project, with a current budget of 12,000 per month. They considered how to divide the money, potentially allocating hours to different domains, and contemplated seeking advice from Void or other sources on structuring salaries and rates (00:52:11). The team also considered potential tax benefits of invoicing from Hungary versus the simplicity of using Dutch accounts, ultimately agreeing that Amir Houieh would propose solutions later (00:54:59).
Website Updates and Technical Tasks: Gabor Kerekes noted that the website primarily needs improvements to typography to increase readability, suggesting changes to font sizes and the potential use of a condensed serif font (00:59:45). Amir Houieh needs to set up a shared Vercel account for the team, and Gabor Kerekes needs to complete the typography fixes and push the changes so Amir Houieh can deploy the website for a final check (01:01:53).
Addressing Civil Project Analytics: The team addressed an outstanding task related to the CBIL project, which requires getting more advanced analytics, specifically including the amount of time users spend in the application (00:49:33) (01:06:21). Gabor Kerekes needs to properly set up the G-Cloud security settings for the team and push the specific analytics script to GitHub, which Amir Houieh will then use to fulfill Noémi Biró's request for updated, detailed exports (01:05:00).
Discussion on App Activity Metrics: Amir Houieh and Noémi Biró discussed the specific analytics needed to measure user activity, specifically the amount of time spent in the app. Noémi Biró indicated that a report previously shared by Gab (Gabor Kerekes) only included last activity, messages by user, and user signups, but lacked data on how many days a user was active. Gabor Kerekes clarified that there are different reports, including a standard weekly one and a more extended analytics report that computes more derived metrics (01:07:27).
Fixing and Routinizing Extended Analytics Reporting: Gabor Kerekes confirmed that the more extended analytics, which calculates derived metrics, was only shared as a draft document. Gabor Kerekes committed to fixing the permissions related to the analytics script and then ensuring that Amir Houieh can also set up and use the script. The goal is to make the export of the extended analytics part of the regular routine (01:07:27).
Suggested next steps
Gabor Kerekes will distill the ideas for the new focus into better words, define a slice, and prepare to start building.
Amir Houieh will move the thoughts about adapt OS to the new focus section on Notion and add Nikun Kotari to the list of investors.
Gabor Kerekes will fix the website typography and push the changes, ensuring to remove debugging handlers.
Amir Houieh will deploy the website changes after Gabor Kerekes pushes them so the group can perform a final check.
Gabor Kerekes will set up the G-Clouds properly by creating a group and adding Amir Houieh and Noémi Biró to ensure they all have the same permissions and push the civil analytics script to GitHub.
Amir Houieh will take care of Melissa's requests regarding the civil analytics once Gabor Kerekes pushes the script to GitHub, using the previous report provided by Noémi Biró as a reference.
Amir Houieh will think about the financial situation and come up with proposals for salaries and rates.
Gabor Kerekes will check if invoicing from Hungary makes more sense for tax reasons.
Gabor Kerekes will fix the permissions for the new reports and ping the group to ensure the setup works for them.
Gabor Kerekes will make the more extended analytics part of the routine to export.
